description: I am high school sophomore student who enjoy exploring the Earth Sciences topic. I am passionate about building interactive websites using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and graphic design. I love working on projects to tackle new challenges involving space and technology.
summary: This innovative map solution enables users to dive into a hands-on experience where they can choose a particular area of interest, select different variables measured by Earth science missions or produced by Earth science models, visualize in a map their current values, how they change over time, and determine what is changing. The Earth science data can be categorized into five major areas: atmosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and cryosphere. The map aims to raise awareness about the importance of earth science . We hope to inspire future generations of scientists and engineers to become passionate about this critical field. With your support, we can enhance the project even further and explore exciting partnership opportunities for outreach and educational initiatives.
details:
What exactly does TerraTracker do?

TerraTracker is an engaging web map that aims to raise awareness about Earth science information through an interactive map tracker. It lets the user choose different parameters to observe and characterize changes in the Earth system. With an easy-to-navigate interface, people can play around with various variables, witnessing the direct effects of that particular variable. There is also an option to view the historical trend of the data over a period of time, thus explaining its impact to the end user.

How does TerraTracker work?

TerraTracker presents Earth science concepts in a clear and engaging way, helping users understand how environmental conditions change over time and how these changes affect our planet.

When users open TerraTracker, they are welcomed by a simple yet interactive dashboard featuring five major Earth systems: the atmosphere, biosphere, geosphere, cryosphere, and hydrosphere. Users can customize their experience by selecting a specific Earth system and choosing the environmental variable they want to explore, such as air temperature, precipitation, or humidity. The interactive map includes a detailed color scale that allows users to interpret the displayed values and identify differences across regions. Additionally, the website clearly identifies the NASA datasets being used, ensuring transparency and helping users understand where the information comes from. By overlaying scientific data onto a geographic map, TerraTracker makes it easier to visualize environmental conditions across different parts of the world.

A panel on the left side of the dashboard provides additional tools for exploring and interpreting the data. Users can select a specific geographic location and adjust the time interval of their observations to daily, monthly, or annual measurements. The panel also includes a detailed trend analysis feature that allows users to examine how environmental variables have changed over time and determine whether those changes are statistically significant. Together, these features make complex Earth science data more accessible and allow users to investigate environmental trends through an interactive and educational experience.

What does TerraTracker hope to achieve?

The goal of this project is to create an engaging and educational platform that helps users better understand the complexities of environmental changes. TerraTracker introduces users to the different factors scientists consider when studying these changes, how environmental data is analyzed, and how significant trends are identified. While scientists use this information to study the impacts of global warming and other environmental changes, TerraTracker makes these insights accessible to everyone by allowing users to explore both current conditions and historical data.

What tools did you use to develop your project?

We utilized a variety of tools and technologies to bring Meteor Matrix Simulator to life:

Development Tools: GitHub, Visual Studio Code, MapLibre for Maps

Languages: Python, React, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Plotly

APIs and Data: APPEEARS  →  Geospatial Data, Giovanni  →  Time Series Data, Hydrology → Hydrological Data, Geo.ca → Canada’s Geospatial, SWOT Mission → Surface water data, NOAA  → Coastwatch and Weather, POWER  →  Weather variables, MODIS / GPM  →  Satellite observations, MERRA-2 / GLDAS  →  Model data

Future Enhancements

There are a few exciting ideas for the TerraTracker's future development:

  • Larger area coverage: Provide the ability to choose a region rather than a single point of interest
  • Better usability: Provide functionality to drag the sidebar to resize the left panel
  • Realistic Models: We aim to enhance accuracy with better models and data sources.
  • User-Friendly Interface: We plan to add educational resources and explanations to improve user understanding.
